messages.author: fa6884457716c3bb
messages.subject: Re: Extract to .mat format
parts:
You can extract several things from the MSImageSet that you would need to do data analysis and visualizations elsewhere:

iData returns the spectral information where m/z is row, and each pixel is columns. You may want to transpose this.  

#get feature matrix from cardinal, feature x pixel
spectra <- iData(dataset)

#transposed, pixel x feature
spectra <- t(iData(dataset))

Getting x,y integer coordinates, if you have additional variables (like "sample") you may want to add more columns to the index, this returns only the xy coordinates
xy_coords =coord(dataset)[,1:2]

To get the m/z values you can use the following, 
mz_values = mz(dataset)

I recommend using an hdf5 format to get the essential data to matlab and I've put a crude example below, there may be better ways to store each piece of data and you may need to set the data types and precisions correctly for each piece of the data to better work with matlab. 
You can get the hdf5 package from Bioconductor ( http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/rhdf5.html):
require(rhdf5)

#make fake dataset
spec <- matrix(runif(9, 0, 1),3,3)
xy <- expand.grid(x=1, y=1:3)
mz <- c(1:3)

#make MSImageSet from fake data
msset <- MSImageSet(spectra = t(spec), coord = xy, mz = mz)

#extract data
specs <- t(iData(msset))

coordinates <- coord(msset)[,1:2]
row.names(coordinates) <- NULL

mz = mz(msset)

#generate h5df for matlab
h5createFile("to_MatlabData.h5")

h5write(spec, "to_MatlabData.h5","spectra")
h5write(xy, "to_MatlabData.h5","coordinates")
h5write(mz, "to_MatlabData.h5","mz")

h5ls("toMatlabData.h5")


h5ls("toMatlabData.h5")

group name otype dclass dim
0 / coordinates H5I_DATASET COMPOUND 3
1 / mz H5I_DATASET INTEGER 3
2 / spectra H5I_DATASET FLOAT 3 x 3

From here see matlab docs: 
https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/hdf5-files.html


Heath Patterson

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Extract to .mat format
parts:
Hi Suhyung,

I cannot help with Matlab, but I assume you may expect the data to be represented as a 3D datacube, with x/y-spatial dimensions and a m/z dimension. However, in Cardinal, the data is stored as a 2D matrix with columns as spectra and rows as flattened images. Using similar code that Heath posted above, you could do:

specs <- imageData(msset)[]

which converts the data into a 3D datacube format that I often see people using for MSI data in Matlab.

Use the select() method to select your tissue region, and then subset the data to eliminate background:

tissue <- select(msset, mz=888) # or whatever m/z can distinguish tissue/background
msset2 <- msset[,tissue]

You can use the reduceDimension() method to bin or resample the m/z values so different images have the same m/z values.

-Kylie

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Extract to .mat format
parts:
If you need to convert the data to a 3D datacube as I suggested, then missing pixels will be converted to 0 automatically whenever that datacube is reconstructed.

If you wish to keep the 2D matrix representation used natively by Cardinal, then you can do:

tissue <- select(msset, mz=888)
spectra(msset)[,!tissue] <- 0

(Note that this may not work if the data is not loaded in memory.)

-Kylie
